cards.text: On the third day, there's a wedding at Cana in Galilee. Jesus' mother is there, and Jesus and His disciples are on the guest list too. Weddings are beautiful, friend, right up until something runs out.

cards.question: Right in the middle of the wedding at Cana, what runs out?
Who comes to Jesus and tells Him, "They have no more wine"?

cards.text: Jesus answers her, "Woman, what is that to you and to Me?" Then He adds, "My hour has not yet come."

cards.question: Jesus tells His mother His hour hasn't come yet. What does she do next?

answers.text: She tells the servants to do whatever He says
She asks the bridegroom to send for more
She sits back down and lets it go

cards.text: Now six stone water jars are sitting right there, set out for the Jewish rites of purification. Each one holds twenty to thirty GALLONS, friend, and my biggest mixing bowl just got real quiet.

cards.question: Jesus turns to the servants and points to those six stone water jars. What does He tell them to do?
The servants fill the six stone jars only halfway.

cards.text: Jesus says, "Now draw some out," and take it to the master of the banquet, the man running the feast. And they just DO it, no questions asked, which is more than I could manage carrying a cup of jar water to the boss.

cards.question: The master of the banquet tastes the water that had been turned into ___.
The master of the banquet knows where the wine came from.
The master of the banquet doesn't know where the wine came from, but the ___ who drew the water know.

cards.text: The master of the banquet calls the bridegroom aside and says, "Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk."

cards.question: Then the master of the banquet tells the bridegroom, "But you have saved the ___ wine until now!"

cards.text: So the bridegroom gets the compliment for a batch he never baked. I KNOW that moment, friend, because that's me every single time the oven does all the work.

cards.question: Turning the water into wine at Cana is the third of Jesus' signs.

cards.text: It's the FIRST of His signs, right there at Cana in Galilee. And with it, He reveals His glory.

cards.question: After this sign at Cana, Jesus' disciples believe in Him.

cards.text: After this, Jesus goes down with His mother, His brothers and His disciples, and they stay a few days.

cards.question: After the wedding at Cana, where does Jesus go down to with His mother, His brothers and His disciples?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "But you have saved the ___ wine until now!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke 'which is more than I could manage carrying a cup of jar water to the boss' does not make sense on a first read. It is unclear what Papa Dorin couldn't manage, or why carrying water to a boss is hard. It does not match the core action, which is servants simply doing what they're told.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank reproduces the master of the banquet's quoted line and asks the baker to supply its missing word. 'Sweet' versus 'fine' is a wording guess, not meaning the baker can reason out. A baker could argue 'sweet' fits the sense of 'the good stuff.'

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card adds no new part of the passage. It restates the master's praise of the bridegroom from cards 13 and 14 (John 2:10) only to carry a joke. Jokes should ride along on a card that moves the passage forward.
'Weddings are beautiful, friend, right up until something runs out' reads as a pleasant, mild line, not a real laugh. The opening card is the best place to set his comic energy.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Story cards 4, 13, 17 and 19 are flat retellings with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice. Across the stop, the only humor is the weak lines on cards 1, 6, 9 and 15. The walkthrough doesn't sound like the laugh-out-loud storyteller the docs describe.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
